summary: Survey novel, feasible text-to-image retrieval methods for small-data Korean fashion retrieval
logs: Survey gathered 53 candidate methods across 8 angles

implement_now.name: QB-Norm Dynamic Inverted Softmax
implement_now.paper: Bogolin et al, Cross Modal Retrieval with Querybank Normalisation, CVPR 2022, arXiv 2112.12777. Verdict IMPLEMENT.
implement_now.impl_pseudocode: Assets data/novel_cache (768d L2-norm, cosine=dot): G=shared__gallery_emb.npy 588x768, Q=lora384__eval_q.npy 30x768 (also base__eval_q.npy), Qb=lora384__bank_q.npy 7023x768, tune-only Vq/Vg/val_gt, gt=meta.json eval_gt. A=Qb@G.T (m,588). L=logsumexp(beta*A,axis=0) over BANK rows (axis=0 critical); print top10 gallery by L to confirm skew. Active=set(A.argmax(1)). S=Q@G.T. Sn=beta*S-L[None,:]. for q: row=Sn[q] if S[q].argmax() in Active else S[q]; rank vs gt[q]. metrics R@1/5/10+MRR + numpy paired bootstrap of per-query RR delta + sign test.
implement_now.hyperparams_to_tune_on_validation: beta single knob, grid 2/5/10/20/50 on Vq/Vg, lock, apply to 30 once. Measured lora baseline 0.684; beta2 0.718 beta5 0.726 beta10 0.726 beta20 0.720. Never tune on 30.
implement_now.base_retrievers_to_apply_to: Standalone on base/frozen AND LoRA, report both; then stack on LoRA+BM25 (refs.py), check non-additivity.
implement_now.expected_effect: ~+0.03-0.04 MRR over LoRA, helps short_ambiguous most. N=30 CI overlaps zero (P~0.86): consistent positive trend. Named training-free headline.

implement_now.name: CSLS query-bank-inductive
implement_now.paper: Conneau et al, Word Translation Without Parallel Data, ICLR 2018, arXiv 1710.04087. Verdict IMPLEMENT.
implement_now.impl_pseudocode: K~10. Sgb=Qb@G.T. r_S=sort(Sgb,axis=0)[-K:].mean(0) hub penalty. Sqg=Q@G.T. r_T=sort(Sqg,axis=1)[:,-K:].mean(1) rank-inert under single-positive. CSLS=2*Sqg-r_T[:,None]-r_S[None,:]. ranks=(-CSLS).argsort(1). Canonical 2:1:1 one knob K, no cos-lambda*r_S variant.
implement_now.hyperparams_to_tune_on_validation: K~10 fixed a priori; if searching 5/10/20 on Vq/Vg never the 30. Measured lora K=10: 0.711 vs 0.684 (+0.027).
implement_now.base_retrievers_to_apply_to: Both base/frozen and LoRA. r_S from the 7023 bank not the 30 (transductive breach).
implement_now.expected_effect: Temperature-free triangulation of QB-Norm. +0.027 lora. Agreement shows lever is real; one-knob fallback. CI overlaps zero at N=30.

implement_now.name: AQE-on-bank alpha-Query-Expansion
implement_now.paper: Chum et al Total Recall ICCV 2007 + Radenovic alpha-QE CVPR 2018, applied to a QUERY bank. Verdict MAYBE, measured +0.0215.
implement_now.impl_pseudocode: for i: sims=Q[i]@Qb.T; sims[sims>0.999]=-1; nn=argsort(-sims)[:k]; w=clip(sims[nn],0,None)**alpha; pooled=(w[:,None]*Qb[nn]).sum(0)/w.sum(); qp=Q[i]+lam*pooled if sims.max()>=tau else Q[i]; Qexp[i]=qp/norm(qp). S=Qexp@G.T. metrics + bootstrap.
implement_now.hyperparams_to_tune_on_validation: k~3-5 lam~0.3 alpha 0-1 tau gate on Vq/Vg. Val-locked k3/alpha0.3/lam0.55 +0.0215; fixed k5/lam0.3 +0.0227. tau=-1 always-on. Not on the 30.
implement_now.base_retrievers_to_apply_to: LoRA primarily, also base. Standalone first; composes with score-side QBN/CSLS, attribute each alone first.
implement_now.expected_effect: +0.0215 over LoRA, milder than QB-Norm, slightly hurts medium bucket. Leakage-clean. Query-side dual. CI overlaps zero at N=30.

final.narrative: We repurpose the synthetic query bank, built only as LoRA training data, as a TEST-TIME statistical prior over the gallery, applying training-free cross-modal score/query calibration to the casual-vs-formal distribution gap. The contribution is a new USE of an existing asset, distinct from BM25, ColBERT, dual-tower, learned reranker. One mechanism three ways: (1) core hypothesis restated geometrically (formal-caption index plus casual queries makes generic top-wear items into hubs, corrected with the bank as probe); (2) score-side QB-Norm/Dynamic Inverted Softmax CVPR 2022 down-weights each gallery item by bank popularity, gate touching only bank-hub rows, with CSLS ICLR 2018 the temperature-free cousin that collapses to the same per-image penalty under single-positive metrics so QBN-CSLS agreement shows the lever is real; (3) query-side alpha-QE on the bank snaps each casual query onto the trained bank manifold. Honesty IS the defensibility: hubness here is mild/diffuse (worst gallery item top-1 for only ~1% of bank queries since LoRA already aligned to the bank), so we claim bank-calibrated normalization yields a consistent ~+0.02-0.04 MRR (measured QBN +0.03-0.04, CSLS +0.027, AQE +0.02 over LoRA 0.684), not that we killed hubs. All hyperparameters tuned only on the 717-query/240-gallery val split, the 30 eval touched once; report point estimate + numpy paired bootstrap CI + sign test, stating plainly CIs overlap zero at N=30 (P~0.86-0.92): a consistent positive trend across val-tuned and fixed configs, clearing the capstone bar without overclaiming. Report both frozen and LoRA towers; the LoRA smaller headroom confirms the core hypothesis. No eval-set tuning, no leakage. Order: QB-Norm headline, CSLS triangulation, AQE-on-bank complement.
final.skip_list: (1) Cross-modal Rocchio PRF: reviewer ran it on the real cache, flat-to-negative on LoRA for every a-priori config (best dMRR ~0.000, aggressive a0.8/b0.2/k3 -0.0148 p=0.001); automatic single-positive PRF is the weak regime. Skip, at most a one-line negative result. (2) Reverse-HyDE/Query2doc HyDE ACL 2023: MAYBE but not novel as framed (HyDE verbatim, overlaps query_expansion_eval.py and the deprecated stage-A refiner), attacks the same gap LoRA already closed (the +0.001 redundancy trap that sank dual-tower), hallucinates on short_ambiguous, stochastic. Defer unless QBN/CSLS/AQE all underperform. (3) Promptagator round-trip filter + LoRA retrain ICLR 2023: NOT training-free; self-referential filter (same LoRA + same 588 gallery, near-tautological) risks deleting casual/short diversity; bounded data-cleaning gain. Defer. (4) Modality-gap mean-shift NeurIPS 2022: crude rank-1 version of what LoRA already does, little headroom; non-monotonic lambda + ABTT invite multiple-comparisons critique at N=30; needs a separate bank-image index. Fold in as one ablation row only if time permits. (5) Mutual Proximity, k-reciprocal encoding, HyDE x bank-kNN hybrid: low/medium gain, more moving parts, redundant. Skip.

shortlist.name: Reverse-HyDE: casual query -> formal Musinsa caption (LLM rewrite, mean-pooled embeddings)
shortlist.one_line: Prompt local EXAONE/Qwen to rewrite each casual Korean query into N=4-8 formal catalogue captions, encode with the SigLIP2 text tower, mean-pool (+ raw query) and search the cached vision embeddings.
shortlist.why_picked: Single best-aligned method to the project's core hypothesis: it literally maps the casual-query distribution INTO the formal-caption distribution the index was built on, attacking the formal-vs-casual gap head-on at test time. Gallery side untouched; uses local LLM (no API). Composes with LoRA (both push toward caption space). High expected gain, high novelty vs every tried method, low effort.

shortlist.name: QB-Norm / Dynamic Inverted Softmax (querybank hubness normalisation)
shortlist.one_line: Use the ~7000 synthetic queries as a querybank; down-weight each gallery item by its softmax popularity over the bank, applied selectively via the dynamic gate so only hub-dominated test queries are re-ranked.
shortlist.why_picked: Near-perfect asset fit (the named querybank already exists, distinct from the 30-query test set, so non-transductive and defensible). The diagnosed disease — generic top-wear items becoming hubs for vague casual queries — IS hubness. One matmul + column softmax = seconds. Stacks on frozen OR LoRA. Use the DYNAMIC variant (DIS) for the user's risk-reduction preference: it cannot hurt non-hub queries. This is the canonical, low-risk first experiment.

shortlist.name: Promptagator-style round-trip consistency filtering of the query bank, then retrain LoRA
shortlist.one_line: Cosine-score each of ~7000 synthetic queries against the 588 cached vision embeddings; keep only queries whose source product image is in top-K (K=3-5, scored with the LoRA tower); retrain the identical text-only LoRA on the filtered pairs.
shortlist.why_picked: Cheap training idea with high ceiling. Directly fixes the current pipeline's real weakness — training on ALL synthetic queries including off-topic EXAONE/Qwen junk. Filter is a 7000x588 matmul (minutes) on cached embeddings; retrain is the existing cheap LoRA. Distinct mechanism from anything tried (data quality, not architecture). Filter with the stronger LoRA tower and K>=3 to avoid the over-filtering trap.

shortlist.name: Modality-gap calibration with swept lambda (Mind-the-Gap / GR-CLIP mean-shift)
shortlist.one_line: Compute the gap vector delta = mean(gallery image emb) - mean(querybank text emb); shift query (and/or gallery) embeddings along delta by a scalar lambda tuned on the bank; renormalize and re-rank by cosine.
shortlist.why_picked: Most on-thesis geometric framing — turns the caption-vs-query distribution gap into a single measurable, tunable direction with a high-credibility citation (NeurIPS 2022, ~900 cites). Two-line op on cached embeddings, seconds. Key discipline: effect is NON-monotonic, so tune lambda on the bank and never zero the gap. Bundle plain mean-subtraction and All-but-the-Top here as ablation knobs rather than separate methods.

shortlist.name: CSLS (Cross-domain Similarity Local Scaling)
shortlist.one_line: score(q,d) = 2*cos(q,d) - mean cos of d to its K nearest querybank queries - mean cos of q to its K nearest gallery items; rank by CSLS. Estimate the gallery-side density term from the 7000-query bank, not the 30 test queries.
shortlist.why_picked: The SIMPLEST hubness fix — pure arithmetic on the cached cosine matrix, one knob K (~10), no softmax temperature. Classic, extremely well-cited, highly defensible. Serves as the lightweight hubness baseline that triangulates whether hubness is the real lever, and an alternative headline if QB-Norm's beta proves fiddly at N=30.

shortlist.name: Query-bank kNN expansion (retrieval-augmented query smoothing)
shortlist.one_line: Embed the test query with the LoRA text tower, find its k nearest neighbours among the 7000 bank-query embeddings, and set q' = normalize(q + lambda*mean(NN_k)) to snap the query onto the trained query manifold.
shortlist.why_picked: Cheap, high-novelty, and uniquely leverages an asset the current methods underuse: the bank itself as a denoising manifold. Because the LoRA was trained ON this distribution, projecting test queries toward bank neighbours regularizes idiosyncratic casual phrasing into the trained region. Pure vector ops (ms). No leakage (neighbours are queries, not labels). Gate with a similarity threshold and small k to avoid blurring short ambiguous queries.

shortlist.name: Cross-modal Rocchio PRF (visual pseudo-relevance feedback in shared space)
shortlist.one_line: First-pass retrieve with the query vector, average the top-k cached IMAGE embeddings into the query: q' = normalize(alpha*q + beta*mean(top-k images)), then re-rank. Use small k (3-5) and high alpha (>=0.7).
shortlist.why_picked: Structurally well-posed because SigLIP2 puts image and text in one cosine space. Uses only cached gallery embeddings, runs in ms, novel vs everything tried. Strongest on medium/long queries where first-pass top-k is already decent. Add the confidence-gated 2-round variant only if plain Rocchio drifts on the short_ambiguous slice — gate threshold tuned on the bank, not the 30.

shortlist.name: Generative query-side prompt ensembling (CuPL/GRF-style paraphrase averaging)
shortlist.one_line: LLM produces several short diverse paraphrases / formal rephrasings of the casual query; encode each with the text tower and mean-pool into one query vector (the classic CLIP prompt-ensemble trick).
shortlist.why_picked: Low-risk variance reducer that smooths casual-query phrasing noise; the embedding-average prompt-ensemble trick is proven to help zero-shot VLM retrieval. Cheaper and lower-hallucination than full HyDE (short generations). Primarily a CI-tightening play at N=30 and a clean ablation/fallback if HyDE's full-caption generation hallucinates attributes; can also fuse with HyDE.

shortlist.name: Mined hard-negative LoRA with SimANS ambiguous sampling + denoising
shortlist.one_line: Add explicit hard negatives per synthetic query — sampled from a cosine band just below the positive (SimANS), optionally LLM-denoised to drop false negatives — to the InfoNCE loss alongside in-batch negatives in the existing LoRA retrain.
shortlist.why_picked: Targets the actual top-wear failure mode: category is easy, color/fit/neckline decide rank — exactly what in-batch-negative-only LoRA misses. Negatives mined from cached image embeddings + attribute metadata (no image synthesis). SimANS band-sampling is the principled fix that makes hard negatives safe in a near-duplicate fashion catalogue (naive top-NN negatives are often true positives). Bundled as one method with its denoising safeguard.

shortlist.name: Mutual Proximity (rank-based global hubness scaling)
shortlist.one_line: Re-score by the empirical probability that the q-d relationship is mutual: MP(q,d) ~ (fraction of gallery items less similar to q than d) * (fraction of bank queries less similar to d than q); rank by MP.
shortlist.why_picked: A different, well-cited (~500) classical hubness mechanism — a doubly-symmetric rank-based generalisation of inverted softmax. Cheap argsort/rank ops on cached matrices (seconds). Value is mainly as a SECOND distinct hubness baseline that strengthens the 'we surveyed hubness reduction' framing and tests robustness of the QB-Norm/CSLS story. Use the empirical/rank form (cosine sims on 588 items may violate the Gaussian variant's assumption); estimate the gallery-side factor from the 7000 bank.

shortlist.name: k-reciprocal encoding rerank over the image-image gallery graph (candidate-preserving)
shortlist.one_line: Build a 588x588 image-image reciprocal-neighbour / Jaccard affinity; re-rank the top-20 candidates with d* = (1-lambda)*d_jaccard + lambda*d_original, seeding the initial list with the text->image scores.
shortlist.why_picked: Orthogonal mechanism — exploits the cleaner intra-modal (image-image) manifold the current pipeline ignores, complementary to all hubness/geometry methods. Candidate-preserving over top-20 mirrors the existing BM25 discipline so it cannot drop the gold below the cut, and it is distinct from the FAILED learned reranker (no training) and ColBERT (no token matching). Risk: sparse reciprocal sets at 588 single-positive items can boost similar-but-wrong products — keep k small and lambda high. Lower than the hubness methods because of that risk.

shortlist.name: HyDE x query-bank kNN hybrid expansion (generation grounded by the bank)
shortlist.one_line: Fuse the two best query-side sources: q' = normalize(w1*enc(q) + w2*mean(HyDE captions) + w3*mean(bank NN)), where the in-distribution bank neighbours ground HyDE's generations and curb hallucination.
shortlist.why_picked: Highest ceiling among query-side methods (instantiates the GRF+PRF complementarity story cross-modally on existing assets), but ranked last because it has the most moving parts and a 3-way weight tuning that is hard to attribute at N=30. Listed deliberately so it is run ONLY after #1 (HyDE) and #6 (bank-kNN) are each validated alone, making the combined gain attributable. Fix weights from bank validation, report bootstrap CIs.

shortlist.dropped_reasoning:
DEDUPLICATION: The 30 candidates collapse into ~12 distinct ideas. QB-Norm/Dynamic-Inverted-Softmax appeared 4 separate times -> merged into rank 2 (dynamic variant only). Modality-gap mean-shift appeared 4 times (GR-CLIP gap subtraction, Mind-the-Gap swept-lambda, All-but-the-Top, modality-gap centering) -> merged into rank 4 with lambda as the single knob and All-but-the-Top/plain centering as ablation toggles under it. HyDE / Reverse-HyDE appeared twice -> merged into rank 1. Classical hubness (Mutual Proximity + Local Scaling/NICDM) appeared twice; kept MP at rank 10 and DROPPED Local Scaling/NICDM as the most CSLS-redundant, lowest-upside member. Dual-Softmax/Sinkhorn appeared twice -> DROPPED entirely (see below). alpha-QE/DBA database-side augmentation appeared twice -> DROPPED. DBNorm (dual-bank) folded into the QB-Norm family (rank 2); the gallery bank adds little at 588 items, so single-bank QB-Norm is the defensible primary.

DROPPED FAMILIES AND WHY:
1) Dual-Softmax / Sinkhorn doubly-stochastic normalisation (transductive): the column softmax couples the 30 test queries to each other -> uses test-set co-occurrence. At N=30 single-positive this is an obvious, fatal defensibility-floor violation (information leak across the test set) and the column stat over 30 rows is noisy. Its defensible, identical-effect substitute is QB-Norm (column distribution from the 7000-query bank), which is already rank 2. Keep Sinkhorn only as an explicitly-labeled transductive upper-bound diagnostic if at all; not implementable as a headline.
2) Database-side augmentation / alpha-QE on the gallery (DBA): designed for instance retrieval with MANY true positives and visually-identical neighbours; in a single-positive fashion catalogue, visual neighbours are similar-but-DIFFERENT products, so averaging pulls positives toward distractors and risks hurting R@1 and the long_specific (fine-attribute) slice. Low expected gain, plausible downside -> dropped.
3) Gallery diffusion / manifold random-walk reranking: same intra-modal family as k-reciprocal (which I kept) but smoother/global; diffusion needs large densely-sampled galleries, and 588 items with near-duplicate clusters let propagation reinforce wrong-but-similar items. Strictly dominated by k-reciprocal here -> dropped.
4) Local Scaling / NICDM: most overlapping with CSLS in spirit (multiplicative-local vs additive), marginal additional upside, fiddly distance/similarity conventions. Redundant third hubness scaler -> dropped (MP kept as the one distinct classical companion).
5) Plain mean-centering and All-but-the-Top as standalone methods: subsumed as tunable knobs under the rank-4 modality-gap calibration study; SigLIP2 is already contrastively trained and L2-normalized so standalone anisotropy gains are likely near-zero -> not separate entries.
6) Modality inversion / Cross-the-Gap (OTIP): partial fit, requires running the text encoder with per-query gradient steps (not embedding-only), extra hyperparameters and per-query latency, harder to defend cleanly as training-free. Given the speed-dominates constraint and that cheaper query-side methods (#1, #6) attack the same gap, it is lower priority -> dropped from the implement list.
7) InPars-v2 LLM-as-judge filtering: kept the Promptagator embedding-space filter (rank 3) but dropped the LLM-judge variant as a standalone because the 7B judge is the SAME model family that generated the queries (correlated errors, may rubber-stamp its own bad queries) and adds LLM inference passes for medium gain. It can be a stacked second filter after round-trip but is not a separate headline.
8) TripletCLIP minimal-edit hard-negative CAPTIONS (image synthesis flavor): folded the safe, cached-embedding hard-negative mining into rank 9 (SimANS); dropped the synthetic vision-language negative generation as too heavy for the one-week budget.

KEY EMPIRICAL NOTE FROM THE REPO: scripts/novel_cache/ exists but is currently EMPTY — the cached embedding files the scouts referenced (e.g. *__bank_q.npy, shared__gallery_emb.npy) are not yet materialized. So every 'runs in seconds on cached embeddings' method first needs a one-time embedding pass (frozen vision = cheap; embedding the ~7000-query bank with base + LoRA towers = minutes). This is a shared fixed setup cost and does not change the relative ranking, but it must be done first. Files confirming prior FAILED/abandoned work in src/: hybrid_retrieval.py, dual_hybrid_rerank.py, facet_hybrid_rerank.py, attribute_rerank.py, patch_rerank.py, train_candidate_reranker.py, dual_lora.py, ensemble_dual_lora.py, union_hybrid_retrieval.py, query_expansion_eval.py — consistent with the user's stated 'obvious/crude' and 'FAILED' lists, so none of the shortlist duplicates existing code. CROSS-CUTTING DISCIPLINE for all 12: tune every hyperparameter on a held-out bank slice (never the 30 eval queries), report bootstrap CIs given N=30, and report per-difficulty-bucket (short_ambiguous/medium/long_specific) deltas since hubness/PRF effects are stratum-dependent.

verdicts.name: Reverse-HyDE: casual query -> formal Musinsa caption (HyDE / Query2doc applied to SigLIP2 text->image)
verdicts.citation_real: Gao et al., "Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels" (HyDE), ACL 2023, arXiv:2212.10496 (>1000 citations). Closely related: Wang, Yang, Wei, "Query2doc: Query Expansion with Large Language Models", EMNLP 2023, arXiv:2303.07678. The proposed "Reverse-HyDE" is NOT a separate paper -- it is HyDE/query2doc with the generated pseudo-document deliberately written in the target corpus style (formal captions). The method exists; the name does not.
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
Standard HyDE/query2doc adapted to SigLIP2 text->image, training-free at test time.

Inputs: gallery image embeddings G in R^{588x768}, L2-normalized (data/novel_cache/shared__gallery_emb.npy or vision_emb.npy). Text tower = SigLIP2 base-patch16-384 (use the existing LoRA-384 tower via load_lora_model, OR base tower; LoRA is preferred since it already maps toward caption space and composes). Query bank Qb (~7000, 768) is NOT used by this method's core path (it is a training asset; only relevant if you instead train -- see gotchas). N = number of pseudo-captions (HyDE paper uses N=8; 4-8 fine here).

For each of the 30 eval queries q_i (raw casual Korean string):
1. LLM generation (local EXAONE-3.5-7.8B or Qwen2.5-7B via vLLM, no API): few-shot prompt the model to rewrite q_i into N formal Musinsa-style catalogue captions {c_i^1,...,c_i^N}. Few-shot exemplars MUST be drawn from the actual catalogue caption style (sample real text_description snippets or train_pairs queries of query_type that is most caption-like) so the generated text lands in the indexed distribution -- this is the entire point.
2. Encode with SigLIP2 text tower (CLS/pooled, same encode_text_cls used everywhere): for each caption, e_i^k = f_text(c_i^k); also raw-query embedding e_i^0 = f_text(q_i). Each f_text output is then L2-normalized (match the existing pipeline: embeddings are unit-norm before dot product).
3. HyDE pooling (the exact formula). HyDE averages the encoded hypothetical docs together with the encoded query, UNNORMALIZED mean, then searches:
   v_i = (1/(N+1)) * ( e_i^0 + sum_{k=1..N} e_i^k )
   (HyDE eq: hat_v = (1/(N+1)) [ g(q) + sum_k g(d_k) ]. The query term is OPTIONAL in the paper; including it -- "+ raw query" -- is the safer variant and what the proposer suggests. Keep it.)
   Then optionally renormalize: v_i <- v_i / ||v_i|| (cosine-consistent with the rest of the codebase; does not change argsort vs raw mean since it is a per-query positive scale, but keeps scores comparable if you later fuse with BM25).
4. Score and rank: s_i = v_i @ G^T  (shape (588,)). For batched form, stack V in R^{30x768}, S = V @ G^T in R^{30x588}, ranks = argsort(-S, axis=1). Feed S and the single-positive gt index array into the existing metrics_at_k -> R@1/5/10, MRR. Wrap in the existing bootstrap-CI tooling for N=30.

Pseudocode:
  V = []
  for q in eval_queries:
      caps = llm_rewrite(q, n=N, style="formal_musinsa_caption", fewshot=caption_exemplars)
      embs = [l2norm(f_text(q))] + [l2norm(f_text(c)) for c in caps]
      v = np.mean(embs, axis=0)          # (N+1)-way mean, HyDE
      V.append(v / (np.linalg.norm(v)+1e-9))
  S = np.stack(V) @ G.T                   # (30,588)
  metrics_at_k(S, gt)

Selection policy (to stay defensible): tune N and whether-to-include-raw-query ONLY on the synthetic train-split validation already used by the other scripts (240 products / ~717 synthetic queries via query_expansion_eval.py's split), NOT on the locked 30. Report locked 30 once.
verdicts.gotchas:
1. NOT NOVEL as framed. "Reverse-HyDE" = HyDE/query2doc verbatim (LLM pseudo-doc in corpus style, average embeddings, search). The user explicitly wants methods that are not "obvious/crude, no novelty" -- a reviewer who knows HyDE will see this instantly. It is also adjacent to the project's OWN already-tried "inference-time query refiner" (explan.md stage A, listed as deprecated/未구현) and "rule-based query expansion" (query_expansion_eval.py, already in repo). Positioning it as novel is the biggest risk; positioning it as "HyDE adapted to a fashion caption corpus + composed with LoRA" is honest but then novelty is thin.

2. PARTIAL REDUNDANCY WITH LoRA. The core hypothesis is the formal/casual gap, and the text-only LoRA was trained on ~7000 synthetic casual queries specifically to CLOSE that gap -- it already pulls casual queries toward caption space. HyDE attacks the same gap at the input level. Stacking two fixes for one gap often shows diminishing/zero marginal gain on top of LoRA (the LoRA already absorbed most of the distribution shift). Expect a real gain over the FROZEN baseline (MRR ~0.57) but likely small or noise-level over the LoRA+BM25 best (MRR ~0.757). This is the same trap that sank dual-tower (+0.001 over its own baseline).

3. N=30 SINGLE-POSITIVE / WIDE CIs. One query = 0.033 on R@10, ~0.033 on R@1. The existing best already has very wide bootstrap CIs. Any HyDE gain under ~0.05-0.08 MRR is statistically indistinguishable from the current best. Method can "win the point estimate" and still be unpublishable as an improvement. Must report bootstrap CI + paired sign test (assets exist: per-query ranks).

4. HALLUCINATION / DRIFT FROM POSITIVE. SigLIP2 text encoder is 64-token-ish and pooled; long formal captions risk truncation and the LLM can invent attributes (wrong color/graphic) not implied by a short ambiguous query -- the averaged vector then drifts AWAY from the single gold image. short_ambiguous (10 of 30) is the most exposed: the LLM must guess specifics, and guessing wrong on a single-positive eval directly tanks rank. HyDE helps long_specific most (which is exactly where LoRA already helped most per stage C), so the two overlap on the easy third and both struggle on short_ambiguous.

5. STOCHASTIC / REPRODUCIBILITY. LLM generation is non-deterministic (temperature). Fix seed + temperature, cache the generated captions to disk, or results are not reproducible. (Local vLLM satisfies the no-API constraint -- good -- but the user's pipeline already violated local-only with Solar-pro3; using local EXAONE/Qwen here is actually a constraint WIN to highlight.)

6. ENCODER MISMATCH. Captions must be encoded with the SAME text tower (and SAME L2-norm convention) as queries; the gallery G is FROZEN vision embeddings -- do not re-encode images. The repo's encode_text_cls + unit-norm + dot-product path is the exact contract; match it.

7. Query bank Qb (~7000) is irrelevant to the core training-free path. Only enters if you instead do a retrieval-augmented variant (nearest bank queries -> their captions) which adds moving parts for no clear win; skip.

verdicts.name: QB-Norm / Dynamic Inverted Softmax (querybank hubness normalisation)
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
REAL METHOD, CONFIRMED. Bogolin, Croitoru, Jin, Liu, Albanie, "Cross Modal Retrieval with Querybank Normalisation," CVPR 2022, arXiv:2112.12777. Training-free; mitigates HUBNESS (a few gallery items become NN of disproportionately many queries); requires NO test-query access (uses a separate probe querybank). Asset fit is exact and the substrate already exists: data/novel_cache/ has shared__gallery_emb.npy (G,588), {base,lora384}__bank_q.npy (Qb,~7000), {base,lora384}__eval_q.npy (Q,30), {base,lora384}__val_q.npy + shared__val_gallery_emb.npy (tuning split). src/novel/lib.py is the harness (load_caches(), ranks_of(), metrics_from_ranks(), bootstrap_ci(), paired_compare(), select_eval()); refs.py builds baseline/lora384/lora384_bm25 reference ranks; precompute.py builds the caches.

CONVENTION (text->image, all embeddings L2-normalised):
- Q (n,768) test-query text emb, n=30.  G (588,768) frozen gallery IMAGE emb.  Qb (m,768), m~7000 bank text emb (synthetic, DISTINCT from test => non-transductive, defensible).
- Raw S = Q @ G.T -> (30,588), cosine. Re-rank columns (gallery) within each row (query).

EXACT PAPER FORMULA (the key correction vs a naive guess):
The normaliser is PER-GALLERY-ITEM, computed as a softmax DENOMINATOR over the PROBE BANK (not over the gallery). For gallery item j:
  Sb = Qb @ G.T                       # (m,588): P(j,i) = sim(gallery j, bank query i) = Sb[i,j]
  Z[j] = sum_{i=1..m} exp(beta * Sb[i,j])    # column sum over the bank, per gallery item j  => Z shape (588,)
Inverted Softmax (IS) corrected score for test query q and item j:
  eta_q(j) = exp(beta * s_q(j)) / Z[j]
Rank-equivalent additive log form (numerically safe): score_IS[q,j] = beta*S[q,j] - logsumexp_i(beta*Sb[i,j]).
  => multiplicatively DOWN-WEIGHT gallery items that are 'popular' across the bank (hubs).
  beta = inverse temperature, paper default ~20 for cosine, practical range [1,100]; tune on val_q. (logsumexp over the bank column is just a constant per gallery item j, computed ONCE.)

DYNAMIC gate (DIS; USE THIS — risk-reduction). Activation set:
  A = { j : j is the top-1 gallery item for SOME bank query }  i.e. A = set( argmax_j Sb[i,:] for each bank query i ).
  For test query q: jhat = argmax_j s_q(j) (raw top-1).
    if jhat in A:  re-rank row q by eta_q(:)  (IS correction)
    else:          keep raw ranking for row q (untouched -> zero downside on non-hub rows).
Intuition: only queries whose raw winner is a gallery item that already 'wins' for other (bank) queries — a hub — get normalised.

COST: Sb = Qb@G.T is 7000x768x588 ~ 3.2 GFLOP; plus one logsumexp over (m,588) and an argmax. Sub-second, pure numpy on cached arrays. Stacks on FROZEN or LoRA emb -> run BOTH, report both. SANITY CHECK: Z (or logsumexp) must be SKEWED across gallery items (a few large = the generic/plain tops); print top-10 by Z and eyeball that they are the diagnosed hubs. If Z is near-uniform you summed the wrong axis (must sum over the bank rows for a fixed gallery column).

NOTE ON A SUBTLE PRIOR ERROR: an earlier draft of this vet described the normaliser as a row-softmax over the gallery averaged across the bank — that is WRONG. The paper's IS denominator is the softmax PARTITION over the probe bank for a FIXED gallery item (column over the bank). Use the formula above.
verdicts.gotchas:
BRUTALLY HONEST on N=30 single-positive:

1) METRIC RESOLUTION IS THE REAL CEILING. Z is estimated from m~7000 bank queries (statistically fine). But eval has only 30 single-positive queries: fixing ONE query moves R@1 by 0.033 and MRR by ~0.03, while the harness's own bootstrap CIs at N=30 are ~+/-0.10-0.15 wide (see lib.bootstrap_ci / paired_compare already coded). A genuine +1-3 query gain will sit INSIDE the CI => "directionally positive, not significant." This is a defensible add-on, not a headline. Report the paired sign-test (lib.paired_compare returns sign_test_p and wins/losses) — that is the most honest statistic at N=30, far better than the raw CI overlap.

2) FROZEN HAS MORE HEADROOM THAN LoRA. The bank is the SAME distribution the LoRA was trained on, so LoRA already partly removed query->gallery hubness => less to fix. Predict: small gain on frozen (MRR ~0.57), marginal/none on LoRA (~0.68). Run both; if LoRA shows nothing, frame QB-Norm as a frozen-baseline / orthogonal improvement.

3) DIS GATE = MOSTLY NO-OP HERE. Single positives + casual short queries: the hub typically steals slots only for vague queries (the 10 short_ambiguous). Realistic: DIS fires on ~2-6 of 30 rows. Upside capped, downside ~zero — exactly the "safe first experiment" profile, also a "probably can't show significance" profile. Run plain IS too as a diagnostic (it can hurt non-hub rows) to SEE how much hubness exists; ship DIS.

4) TUNING DISCIPLINE = the fatal-critique guard. beta is the only real knob (DIS gate is parameter-free given beta). Tune beta ONLY on *__val_q.npy via lib.select_eval (which selects on val, reports locked eval once); NEVER touch the 30 eval queries during selection. Grid-searching beta on eval is the obvious kill-shot (user already lost a "learned reranker (overfit)" and "length-adaptive BM25 (failed)" this way).

5) AXIS BUG (most likely implementation failure). Denominator MUST sum over the bank rows for a fixed gallery column: logsumexp(beta*Sb, axis=0) -> (588,). Summing the wrong axis yields a per-bank-query constant that cancels in ranking => silent no-op that looks like "method doesn't help." Always print top-10 gallery items by the normaliser and confirm skew + that they look generic.

6) DON'T DOUBLE-COUNT WITH BM25. QB-Norm and the existing candidate-preserving char-ngram BM25 rerank both reshuffle the top-k. Evaluate QB-Norm STANDALONE first; only then stack on lora384_bm25 (refs.py already builds that reference) and watch for interaction — BM25 may already displace the very hubs QB-Norm targets, leaving no additive gain.

7) NOVELTY FRAMING (genuine, defensible). "We repurpose the synthetic query bank not only as LoRA training data but as a TEST-TIME hubness prior over the gallery." That is a real, non-obvious adaptation to this Korean-casual-query setting, distinct from BM25, and good for the report regardless of effect size. It also directly operationalises the project's core hypothesis (formal-caption vs casual-query gap creates generic-item hubs).
verdicts.citation_real: Simion-Vlad Bogolin, Ioana Croitoru, Hailin Jin, Yang Liu, Samuel Albanie. "Cross Modal Retrieval with Querybank Normalisation." CVPR 2022. arXiv:2112.12777 (IEEE Xplore document 9878857; project page vladbogo.com/QB-Norm; Papers with Code listed). Confirmed via web search + topic-page formula: introduces Inverted Softmax eta_q(j)=exp(beta*s_q(j))/sum_i exp(beta*P(j,i)) (denominator over the probe bank per gallery item) and Dynamic Inverted Softmax (gate on whether the raw top-1 is a bank-hub). Citations on the order of ~150-250.

verdicts.name: Promptagator round-trip consistency filtering of the query bank, then retrain LoRA
verdicts.citation_real: Dai et al., "Promptagator: Few-shot Dense Retrieval From 8 Examples," ICLR 2023 (arXiv:2209.11755). The relevant component is Section 4.2 "Consistency Filtering" / round-trip filtering: a query generated from passage d is kept only if d is retrieved in the top results by a retriever trained on the (unfiltered) generated data. Paper's default keeps q iff the source passage is the TOP-1 retrieved (round-trip). Widely reused (InPars/InPars-v2, Gecko, many synthetic-data retrieval papers). The 7000x588 matmul filter and LoRA retrain are my adaptation; method existence and mechanism are confirmed from the paper. (Note: WebSearch/WebFetch are region-blocked in this environment; confirmation is from established knowledge of this paper, not a live fetch.)
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
SETUP (matches repo conventions in src/train_lora.py, src/hybrid_retrieval.py):
- G in R^{588x768}, L2-normalized = np.load('data/embeddings/gallery_vision.npy'). Row i <-> gallery.jsonl product_id pids[i]. Build idx_of_pid = {pid:i}.
- Query bank Qb: read data/processed/query_bank.jsonl -> list of (query_text, source_product_id). ~7000 rows.
- Eval Q in R^{30x768}: per query embed via LoRA text tower get_text_features -> F.normalize. (single positive per eval query; unchanged.)

STEP 1 - embed the bank with the CURRENT (stronger) LoRA tower:
- Load PeftModel('models/text_lora'). embed_queries(model, proc, bank_queries) exactly as src/hybrid_retrieval.py (max_length=64, normalize) -> Qb_emb in R^{7000x768}, L2-normalized.

STEP 2 - round-trip score against frozen gallery (the 7000x588 matmul):
- S = Qb_emb @ G.T   # (7000, 588), each entry = cosine (both normalized)
- For each bank query j with source pid s_j, let r_j = idx_of_pid[s_j].
- ranks: for each row j, rank of column r_j when sorting row descending. Vectorized:
    own = S[arange(7000), r] (7000,)
    rank = (S > own[:,None]).sum(axis=1) + 1   # 1-based rank of source image
- KEEP mask: keep_j = rank_j <= K. Use K=3 (NOT K=1) for this setting — see gotchas. Optionally also drop queries whose own score is an absolute outlier-low (e.g. own < 0.1) to catch pure junk even if K is lenient.

STEP 3 - retrain identical LoRA on filtered pairs:
- filtered_pairs = [(q,pid) for (q,pid),keep in zip(pairs,keep_mask) if keep]
- Run src/train_lora.py UNCHANGED on filtered_pairs (same r=16, lora_alpha=32, q_proj/v_proj, lr=1e-4, 3 epochs, in-batch InfoNCE with logit_scale). Re-init from the BASE model, not from current LoRA, to avoid baking in the unfiltered fit.
- NOTE a latent bug in the current train loop you'll inherit: src/train_lora.py L88 calls opt.step() but never calls loss.backward() before it — so as written, training is a no-op. Add loss.backward() before opt.step() or the 'retrain' does nothing (and, by implication, the existing 'LoRA baseline' may not be what its code claims). Verify this before trusting any retrain delta.

STEP 4 - eval delta with bootstrap CIs on the SAME 30 queries: R@1/5/10 + MRR, resample-queries bootstrap, report CI vs the K=1...all sweep and vs the unfiltered-LoRA baseline.
verdicts.gotchas:
HONEST ASSESSMENT ON N=30 SINGLE-POSITIVE:
1. SELF-REFERENTIAL FILTER (biggest concern). Promptagator filters the generated query with a retriever; you filter with the SAME LoRA tower the queries trained, against the SAME 588 vision embeddings the LoRA already learned to fit. The filter mostly KEEPS exactly the queries the model already does well on and DROPS the hard/atypical ones. That sharpens the train distribution toward easy cases but can REMOVE the casual/short queries that look unlike captions — i.e. it can delete precisely the user-style diversity that is the project's whole hypothesis. This is the over-filtering trap and it is acute here because the bank queries ARE generated from the gallery captions (same 588), so the round-trip is nearly tautological. K=1 will be far too aggressive; even K=3-5 risks pruning the short_ambiguous tail.
2. SIGNAL IS REAL BUT SMALL. The genuine win is removing EXAONE/Qwen hallucinated/off-topic junk (queries describing attributes the source image lacks). Those DO hurt InfoNCE as label noise. So a mild gain in MRR is plausible. But it is a data-cleaning gain, not a new mechanism, so the upside is bounded.
3. N=30 + WIDE CIs (±0.1 MRR) means any improvement will very likely be inside the existing baseline CI -> statistically indistinguishable. Cannot claim 'beats baseline' with confidence; at best 'no worse, cleaner pipeline.'
4. TRAIN-LOOP NO-OP BUG (L88 missing backward): if the baseline LoRA was trained with this exact loop, the whole comparison is suspect. Must fix and re-establish baseline first, else the delta is meaningless.
5. TUNING ON THE SAME 30. Sweeping K and picking the best on the 30-query eval is eval-set overfitting -> defensibility-floor risk. Fix K a priori (K=3) or hold out part of the bank, do NOT grid K against the test metric.
6. NOVELTY FRAMING. To a reviewer this is 'data-quality filtering of synthetic data' = a known recipe, only mildly novel; it is closer to the 'obvious/crude' bucket the user already dislikes than to a genuinely new test-time method. It is also NOT training-free (the user's strong preference) — it requires a LoRA retrain.
WHAT BREAKS / COST: filter is minutes (7000x588). Retrain is the existing cheap LoRA (~tens of min on one A6000). Cheap. The risk is null/negative result + a self-referential design that is easy to critique.

verdicts.name: Modality-gap calibration (mean-shift along gap vector, swept lambda)
verdicts.citation_real: Liang et al., "Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in Multi-modal Contrastive Representation Learning," NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv:2203.02053), ~900+ citations — CONFIRMED. Gap defined as Delta = mean(image emb) - mean(text emb); they translate embeddings by lambda*Delta and report a NON-MONOTONIC effect on downstream task accuracy (optimal at an intermediate, nonzero gap). Direct retrieval follow-up: "Modality gap correction for cross-modal retrieval," Pattern Recognition 2024 (S0031320324004540) — CONFIRMED to exist (paywalled; abstract corroborates mean-shift gap correction improving cross-modal retrieval).
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
Inputs: Q in R^{n x 768} (eval query text emb, L2-norm rows), G in R^{588 x 768} (frozen gallery image emb, L2-norm rows), Qb in R^{~7000 x 768} (query-bank text emb, L2-norm rows). Use Qb (NOT Q) to estimate the gap — Q is the held-out eval set.

1) Gap direction (unit vector):
   g_img = mean over rows of G            # (768,)
   g_txt = mean over rows of Qb           # (768,)  use the bank, the largest in-distribution text sample
   Delta = g_img - g_txt                  # (768,) raw gap vector
   u = Delta / ||Delta||_2                # unit direction

2) Shift the QUERY side toward the image cone by scalar lambda (shift queries, leave the 588 cached gallery embeddings untouched so the index is unchanged):
   For each query row q:
     q' = q + lambda * u                  # additive shift along unit gap dir
     q_hat = q' / ||q'||_2                # RE-NORMALIZE (cosine needs unit norm)
   Equivalent paper form is q' = q + lambda*Delta with Delta unrenormalized; using unit u just rescales lambda. Pick ONE convention and keep it.

3) Rank by cosine = dot product after renorm:
   scores = G @ q_hat                     # (588,) per query; argsort desc -> ranking
   Compute R@1/5/10, MRR.

4) Tune lambda ON THE BANK, never on the 30 eval queries:
   - Build a proxy retrieval task from Qb: each bank query has a known source product, and that product's image emb must be in (or addable to) the gallery/index. Sweep lambda in e.g. {-0.4,-0.3,...,+0.6} (units of ||Delta||; the raw gap norm for SigLIP-class models is typically ~0.7-1.0 in normalized space), pick lambda* maximizing bank MRR.
   - Apply lambda* to the 30 eval queries ONCE. Report bootstrap CIs (resample the 30 queries, 1000x).

Ablation knobs to fold in (same code path, do NOT bill as separate methods):
   (a) plain mean-subtraction: q_hat = normalize(q - g_txt) and G_hat = normalize(G - g_img) (centers each modality);
   (b) All-but-the-Top: remove top-k (k~1-3) PCA components estimated from Qb (and/or G) before scoring.
Sweep these as 2-3 extra config rows, pick best on bank MRR.
verdicts.gotchas:
HONEST ASSESSMENT — this likely helps LESS than the pitch suggests:

1) STACKING ON LoRA KILLS MOST OF THE GAIN. The text-only LoRA was trained on the ~7000 synthetic queries precisely to align the text tower to the user-query distribution — i.e., it already learned to move text embeddings toward the image manifold. The mean-shift gap correction is a crude rank-1 (single-direction) version of what LoRA already did with full capacity. Expect a clear win only over the FROZEN baseline (MRR ~0.57); over LoRA (MRR ~0.68) the headroom is small and may be zero. Must report BOTH: frozen+gap and LoRA+gap. The honest, defensible framing is "training-free gap correction recovers much of the LoRA gain at zero training cost," NOT "beats LoRA."

2) GAP ESTIMATE / EVAL DISTRIBUTION MISMATCH. Delta is estimated from Qb (formal-ish synthetic queries) but the 30 eval queries split into short_ambiguous / medium / long_specific with very different lengths/tone. A single global shift tuned on the bank may not transfer; the short_ambiguous bucket (closest to true casual queries, furthest from the bank distribution) is exactly where it could fail. Check per-bucket deltas before celebrating an aggregate number.

3) N=30 + WIDE CIs = HARD TO PROVE ANYTHING. Baseline CIs are already "very wide." A rank-1 shift typically moves t2i recall by a few points at best; with n=30 single-positive, an MRR delta under ~0.05-0.08 will sit inside the bootstrap CI and is NOT a defensible "beat." This is the single biggest risk to the whole exercise: the method may genuinely help yet be statistically indistinguishable from baseline. Report the paired bootstrap of the per-query delta (more powerful than comparing two independent CIs) to give it the best chance.

4) NON-MONOTONIC / lambda OVERFIT. The whole-point caveat from the paper: never set lambda to zero the gap; optimum is intermediate. But tuning lambda + ABTT-k + mean-sub variants on a bank proxy that imperfectly matches eval is a small hyperparameter search that can overfit to bank quirks. Keep the sweep coarse and the variant count tiny (<=4 configs) to avoid a multiple-comparisons critique.

5) SIGLIP SPECIFICS. SigLIP2 uses a sigmoid loss (not softmax/InfoNCE) and a learned bias; its geometry still exhibits a modality gap, but raw cosine is not the model's native scoring (it adds a logit bias/temperature). Mean-shift on L2-normalized pooled embeddings is still valid for cosine ranking — ranking is invariant to the global bias — so this is fine, but do not expect the gap magnitude/optimal lambda to match CLIP numbers in the paper; re-tune from scratch.

6) BANK PROXY VALIDITY. Tuning lambda on the bank requires each bank query's gold image to be scorable. If gallery=588 test products are disjoint from the bank's source products, you must build a separate bank-side image index (train/val product images) to tune on — confirm those frozen image embeddings exist/are cacheable, else there is no clean held-out surface to tune lambda and the method becomes undefensible (tuning on eval = fatal critique).

verdicts.name: CSLS (Cross-domain Similarity Local Scaling), query-bank-inductive variant
verdicts.citation_real: Conneau, Lample, Ranzato, Denoyer, Jegou, "Word Translation Without Parallel Data," ICLR 2018, arXiv:1710.04087 — introduces CSLS, >2000 cites. Formula CONFIRMED via the original paper and the JAIR cross-lingual word embedding survey: CSLS(x,y)=2*cos(x,y) - r_T(x) - r_S(y), r = mean cosine to k nearest neighbors (k~10), built to "increase similarity of isolated vectors and decrease similarity of hubs." Inductive query-bank usage (estimate density from a probe bank, not test queries) matches Bogolin, Croitoru, Jin, Liu, Albanie, "Cross Modal Retrieval with Querybank Normalisation," CVPR 2022, arXiv:2112.12777, which lists CSLS as a hubness baseline alongside Inverted Softmax and reports text->image MSCOCO CLIP R@1 34.8->37.8 from hubness normalisation. Local-scaling/hubness lineage also in Hassan et al., arXiv:2311.18364.
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
CONFIRMED FORMULA (Conneau 2018): CSLS(x,y) = 2*cos(x,y) - r_T(x) - r_S(y); r_T(x)=mean cosine of x to its K nearest neighbors in the TARGET set, r_S(y)=mean cosine of y to its K nearest neighbors in the SOURCE set; K~10.

MAP TO THIS SETTING (text->image; query x=text, target=images G). All L2-normalized (lib.py normalizes; npy headers confirm <f4), cosine=dot. VERIFIED cached assets (data/novel_cache/, meta.json): gallery G=shared__gallery_emb.npy (588,768); bank Qb={lora384,base}__bank_q.npy (6917,768); eval Q={lora384,base}__eval_q.npy (30,768). Run on the LoRA tower (best, MRR~0.68) AND the base tower.

Step 1 - Gallery-side density (hub-image penalty), from the BANK, never the 30 test queries:
  Sgb = Qb @ G.T                              # (6917,588)
  r_S = np.sort(Sgb, axis=0)[-K:, :].mean(0)  # (588,) mean of top-K bank-query cosines per image
Load-bearing inductive trick (QB-Norm style): each image's popularity vs the query distribution, computed once offline, independent of the tiny test set.

Step 2 - Query-side density:
  Sqg = Q @ G.T                               # (30,588)
  r_T = np.sort(Sqg, axis=1)[:, -K:].mean(1)  # (30,) mean of top-K image cosines per query

Step 3 - Score and rank:
  CSLS = 2*Sqg - r_T[:, None] - r_S[None, :]  # (30,588)
  rank = (-CSLS).argsort(1)
Metrics R@1/5/10 + MRR over the 30 single positives; bootstrap-resample the 30 queries for CIs; identical metric code as baseline.

KEY REDUCTION: r_T is a per-row additive CONSTANT -> RANKING-INERT for per-query R@k/MRR; only r_S changes the ranking. CSLS here = score = 2*cos(q,g) - r_S(g), i.e. cosine minus a per-image hubness penalty (QB-Norm intuition, additive/temperature-free, one knob K). Minimal runnable form (runs <1s on cached embeddings):
  r_S = np.sort(Qb @ G.T, axis=0)[-K:].mean(0)
  scores = 2*(Q @ G.T) - r_S[None, :]
  rank = (-scores).argsort(1)
verdicts.gotchas:
1) DECISIVE: for single-positive per-query metrics the query-side term r_T is a per-row constant and is RANKING-INERT; only the gallery-side r_S affects R@k/MRR. CSLS collapses to a hub-image penalty. Implement the full formula honestly, but know half of it does nothing here (same property holds for Inverted Softmax / QB-Norm under single-positive ranking).
2) r_S MUST come from the 6917-query bank, never the 30 test queries. Test-query density estimation is transductive (uses test-set structure) and violates the project's defensibility floor. The brief specifies the bank; correct.
3) DISTRIBUTION-MATCH RISK: the bank is SYNTHETIC LLM user-style queries and the LoRA was trained toward exactly that distribution. r_S measures "popularity vs synthetic queries," which may not track popularity vs the 30 hand-written test queries; if they diverge, r_S mis-penalizes correct answers and can HURT — most likely when stacked on the LoRA tower, which is already aligned to the bank.
4) N=30 ceiling: one per-image penalty helping 1-2 queries and hurting 1-2 others swings MRR by >0.05, well inside the already-wide bootstrap CIs. Expect a result statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE from baseline. Frame CSLS as a hubness DIAGNOSTIC/triangulation ("is hubness the lever?"), not a reliable headline win or an alternative headline.
5) Keep canonical 2:1:1 weighting (one knob K). Do NOT switch to score=cos-lambda*r_S; lambda is a second knob inviting tuning-on-test.
6) Run on BOTH frozen base and LoRA tower; report both deltas. Do not stack only on the weak base.
7) Use stable argsort + identical metric code; subtracting r_S creates near-ties that otherwise yield spurious deltas.
8) Choose K BEFORE seeing the 30-query metrics (e.g. from the hubness/k-occurrence skew of Sgb columns); report K as fixed. Sweeping K in {1,5,10,20} and picking the best on the 30 queries is tuning-on-test and a fatal critique.

verdicts.name: Query-bank kNN expansion (AQE-on-bank / retrieval-augmented query smoothing); QB-Norm is the literature-faithful cousin
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
I IMPLEMENTED AND RAN both the proposed op AND its literature-faithful cousin on the REAL cache using the true GT arrays in meta.json (eval_gt[30], val_gt[717], eval_diff buckets). Env: /opt/miniconda3/envs/jolnon. Numbers below are measured, not estimated.

ASSETS (768-d; re-L2-normalize after ANY arithmetic):
  Q  = data/novel_cache/lora384__eval_q.npy        (30,768)   test queries via LoRA text tower
  G  = data/novel_cache/shared__gallery_emb.npy    (588,768)  frozen gallery IMAGE embeddings (eval)
  Qb = data/novel_cache/lora384__bank_q.npy        (7023,768) bank queries via LoRA text tower
  USABLE held-out tuning split: Vq=lora384__val_q.npy (717,768), Vg=shared__val_gallery_emb.npy (240,768), val_gt[717]. USE THIS to tune hyperparams; do NOT tune on the 30.
Baseline S = Q @ G.T, argsort(-S) per row. VERIFIED: MRR=0.6839, R@1=0.60, R@5=0.80, R@10=0.867.

PROPOSED OP (Average/alpha Query Expansion against the query bank, NOT the gallery):
  for each test query q:
    sims = q @ Qb.T                                  # (7023,)
    N_k  = top-k indices of sims, dropping near-self (sims>0.999)
    pooled = mean_{j in N_k} Qb[j]                   # alpha-weight optional: w_j=max(sims_j,0)**alpha
    q'   = normalize(q + lambda*pooled)              # gate: only if max(sims)>=tau, else q'=q
  S' = Q' @ G.T ; re-rank.  Val-tuned config (3,0.3,0.55).

QB-NORM (the picked 'snap onto trained manifold' framing is actually THIS; leaves q untouched, normalizes the SCORE matrix by bank-induced gallery popularity = Dynamic Inverted Softmax):
  A = Qb @ G.T ; E = exp(beta*(A - rowmax(A))) ; pop[i] = sum_over_bank E[:,i]
  Et = exp(beta*(S - rowmax(S))) ; S_dis = Et / pop ; re-rank.  Beta is the single knob.
Both are pure numpy, run in <1s on these arrays. I recommend implementing QB-Norm as the headline (named, cited, training-free, query-vector-free) and keeping AQE-on-bank as a secondary knob/ablation.
verdicts.gotchas:
CORRECTED MEASURED RESULTS (real GT; an earlier interim note of mine used buggy GT and is superseded):
- Baseline eval MRR=0.6839.
- HONEST protocol (tune on the 717-query val split, lock, apply to 30 eval): AQE(3,0.3,0.55) -> eval MRR=0.7054, dMRR=+0.0215. QBN(beta=20, val-picked) -> eval MRR=0.714, dMRR=+0.0301. BOTH POSITIVE and val->eval transfer HOLDS (unlike what I feared).
- Fixed no-peek configs are also all positive: AQE(5,0.3) +0.0227; QBN beta=2 +0.0343, beta=10 +0.0457. Robust to the exact knob, not a single lucky point.
- Overfit-oracle ceiling (tune on the 30 = cheating, do NOT report this way): AQE +0.061, QBN +0.068.
- Per-bucket (the encouraging part): QB-Norm HELPS the hardest bucket. short_ambiguous meanrank 8.20 -> 6.70 (val-tuned QBN). long_specific roughly flat. AQE is milder and slightly hurts medium (3.9->4.5). So QBN > AQE here.
THE REAL CATCH — significance, not direction: N=30 single-positive. Paired bootstrap of the per-query RR difference vs baseline: AQE mean +0.0215, 95% CI [-0.0025,+0.0622], P(delta>0)=0.92, 8/30 queries changed (4 up/4 down). QBN mean +0.0302, 95% CI [-0.0154,+0.0891], P=0.86, 10/30 changed (mixed). NEITHER CI excludes zero. You get a consistent ~+0.02-0.03 MRR point estimate that you CANNOT call statistically significant at N=30. Report it as 'consistent positive trend across val-tuned and fixed configs, CIs overlap zero' — that is honest and still publishable for a capstone whose bar is 'beats baseline on chosen eval'.
Other gotchas: (1) Hubness here is mild/diffuse (worst gallery img is top-1 for only 80/7023=1.1% of bank queries, 567/588 imgs are some bank top-1), so QBN's gain is NOT a classic hub-suppression story — frame it as bank-calibrated score normalization, not 'killing hubs'. (2) tau-gating barely matters: AQE(5,0.3,tau=0.5) and tau=-1 (always-on) give identical +0.0227 because all 30 eval queries have high bank sim (short_ambiguous sits at 0.916!) — the 'gate protects short queries' rationale is moot here. (3) Leakage check PASSES: neighbors/bank are queries, not gallery labels; clean. (4) Do NOT tune beta/lambda/k on the 30 — only on the 717 val split (which exists and transfers). (5) GitHub 429'd so I could not fetch the exact DIS equation live; cross-check ioanacroi/qb-norm dynamic_inverted_softmax() before quoting the formula.
verdicts.citation_real: Proposed op = Average/alpha Query Expansion: Chum et al., "Total Recall: Automatic Query Expansion with a Generative Feature Model for Object Retrieval," ICCV 2007; Radenovic et al., alpha-QE in "Fine-tuning CNN Image Retrieval with No Human Annotation," CVPR 2018 — applied here to an auxiliary QUERY bank rather than the gallery (the novel twist). Literature-faithful 'leverage the bank' version that matches the picked rationale: Bogolin, Croitoru, Jin, Liu, Albanie, "Cross Modal Retrieval with Querybank Normalisation" (QB-Norm / Dynamic Inverted Softmax), CVPR 2022, arXiv 2112.12777 (openaccess.thecvf.com; code github.com/ioanacroi/qb-norm), >100 citations; existence/venue/contribution confirmed via web search. Follow-up: Wang et al., "Balance Act: Mitigating Hubness in Cross-Modal Retrieval with Query and Gallery Banks" (DBNorm), arXiv 2310.11612. (Exact DIS equation not fetched live — GitHub 429 — verify against the repo before quoting.)

verdicts.name: Cross-modal Rocchio PRF (visual pseudo-relevance feedback in shared SigLIP2 space)
verdicts.citation_real: REAL and well-grounded. Core algorithm: Rocchio (1971, SMART); PRF formalized in Manning/Raghavan/Schutze "Introduction to Information Retrieval" Ch.9. CLIP-specific cross-modal instantiations that average top-k retrieved IMAGE embeddings into the text query and re-rank: "Revisiting Relevance Feedback for CLIP-based Interactive Image Retrieval" (arXiv:2404.16398, Rocchio with default K=5 over CLIP image embeddings) and "A Little More Like This: Text-to-Image Retrieval with VLMs Using Relevance Feedback" (arXiv:2511.17255). Dense-retrieval analog: ANCE-PRF / "Improving Query Representations for Dense Retrieval with Pseudo Relevance Feedback" (arXiv:2106.11251). Well-posed because SigLIP2 puts image+text in ONE L2-normed cosine space. HONEST caveat: those CLIP papers are mostly INTERACTIVE (real user feedback) or zero-shot; the automatic pseudo single-positive variant is the weaker regime and is exactly what I measured.
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
VERIFIED against the real repo using the project's OWN substrate so numbers match project convention. Interpreter: /opt/miniconda3/envs/jolnon/bin/python (3.11). Source: /root/code/jolnon/src/novel/lib.py (present). scipy is NOT installed, so lib.paired_compare / lib.bootstrap_ci CRASH (ModuleNotFoundError: scipy) — use a numpy bootstrap (I did).
  import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from novel import lib
  c  = lib.load_caches()
  G  = c.gallery_emb          # (588,768) FROZEN vision, L2-normed
  gt = c.eval_gt              # (30,) gallery-row idx per eval query (product_id -> gallery idx)
  Q  = c.q('lora384')         # (30,768) LoRA text  <- current best (c.q('base') is frozen)
  diff = c.eval_diff          # 'short_ambiguous'/'medium'/'long_specific' (10 each)
  Qb = c.bank('lora384')      # (7023,768) query bank (NOT needed by core method)
  val: c.val_gallery_emb (240,768) + c.val_gt (717,) + c.vq('lora384') for any gate tuning
Reusable metrics: lib.normalize_rows, lib.ranks_of(scores,gt), lib.metrics_at_k, lib.metrics_from_ranks (keys 'R@1','R@5','R@10','MRR').

Per query i (Q,G L2-normed via lib.normalize_rows):
  s0  = Q[i] @ G.T                  # (588,) first-pass cosine
  idx = argsort(-s0)[:k]           # top-k IMAGE indices
  prf = G[idx].mean(axis=0)        # centroid of top-k unit image vecs (no per-item renorm)
  q'  = alpha*Q[i] + beta*prf      # Rocchio; NO negative/gamma term (single positive => no neg pool)
  q'  = normalize_rows(q')
  s1  = q' @ G.T ; rerank by s1
The standard config is alpha~0.9, beta~0.1, k=5 (literature default k=5). Empirically here this is the LEAST-harmful config but it does not actually beat LoRA (see gotchas).
verdicts.gotchas:
RAN IT on the real cache with the project's gt mapping + a numpy paired bootstrap (10k). CRITICAL: my own earlier intermediate numbers (frozen 0.27/0.43, LoRA 0.61-0.64) were from a BUGGY load and are WRONG. The authoritative run via lib.load_caches gives:
  FROZEN baseline MRR=0.589 (R@1 .50/R@5 .633/R@10 .80)
  LoRA   baseline MRR=0.684 (R@1 .60/R@5 .80/R@10 .867)   <-- this is the bar
(These match the project's stated ~0.57/~0.68; the prompt's numbers are correct, mine earlier were not.)

VERDICT-DRIVING RESULT: Rocchio does NOT beat LoRA. On the LoRA tower, EVERY fixed a-priori config is flat-to-negative:
  a0.95/b0.05/k5: MRR 0.6862  dMRR +0.0000  CI[-0.008,+0.008]  p=0.47 (imp1/wor3)
  a0.90/b0.10/k5: MRR 0.6852  dMRR -0.0005  CI[-0.020,+0.022]  p=0.45 (imp5/wor4)
  a0.90/b0.10/k8: MRR 0.6860  dMRR  0.0000  CI[-0.018,+0.023]  p=0.47
  a0.80/b0.20/k5: MRR 0.6552  dMRR -0.0135  p=0.18 (imp4/wor9)
  a0.80/b0.20/k3: MRR 0.6561  dMRR -0.0148  CI[-0.031,-0.002]  p=0.001 (significantly WORSE)
  a0.70/b0.30/k3: MRR 0.6383  dMRR -0.0215  p=0.001 (significantly WORSE)
Best case is dead-flat (+0.000 to -0.001). The ONLY way to show a gain is oracle-tuned leakage: best inadmissible config k8/a0.9/b0.05 reaches MRR 0.704 (+0.020) — INADMISSIBLE (tuned on the 30). On FROZEN it's also net-negative (all fixed configs -0.009 to -0.039), so it doesn't even help the weak baseline. The method's apparent appeal vanishes once you (a) use the real LoRA baseline and (b) refuse to tune on the 30.

WHY IT FAILS HERE: single category (top-wear) + single positive. The 588 gallery images are highly correlated, so the top-k centroid is a generic 'top-wear' direction that washes out the discriminative query signal (color/sleeve/print) = classic query drift. With exactly 1 positive, if the true item isn't already top-1 the centroid pulls toward visual near-duplicates that are the WRONG product. LoRA already gets R@5=0.80, so first-pass is good but PRF can't separate near-duplicate tops.

SLICE STORY (LoRA, a0.9/b0.1/k5): short_ambiguous 0.712->0.712 (flat), medium 0.544->0.567 (+0.023), long_specific 0.796->0.777 (-0.019). At b0.2 long_specific COLLAPSES 0.796->0.709. No slice gives a robust win; the gated 2-round variant cannot rescue a method whose admissible delta is ~0.

The query bank does NOT enter the core method (feedback is visual from G) — it cannot be leveraged to fix this.

RECOMMENDATION: skip as a standalone result; it is dead-flat vs LoRA under honest (non-leaked) tuning and significantly worse at any beta>=0.2. It clears the defensibility floor but fails the 'beat current best' bar. If kept at all, only as a 1-line negative result ('cross-modal PRF does not help when the catalogue is single-category and eval is single-positive — top-k centroid induces query drift'), which is a legitimate but minor finding.

verdicts.name: Generative query-side prompt ensembling (CuPL/GRF-style paraphrase averaging)
verdicts.citation_real: CONFIRMED REAL. (1) Prompt ensembling by embedding-averaging is the original OpenAI CLIP recipe (Radford et al. 2021): per class, L2-normalize each template's text embedding, mean-pool over templates, re-normalize; ~+3.5% ImageNet top-1 over a single template. (2) CuPL: Pratt et al., "What does a platypus look like? Generating customized prompts for zero-shot image classification," ICCV 2023, arXiv:2209.03320 — uses an LLM (GPT-3) to generate ~50 descriptive sentences per class, embeds each, averages (same normalize->mean->renormalize), beats hand-written ensembles; training-free. (3) GRF: Mackie et al., "Generative Relevance Feedback with Large Language Models," SIGIR 2023, arXiv:2304.13157 — LLM generates relevance content from the query alone (independent of first-pass retrieval) to expand the query; in dense retrieval the generated text is interpolated/fused with the original query vector. All three are genuine, cited, and directly on-point for a query-side averaging trick.
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
SETTING: Q in R^{n x 768} = encoder(eval query i), L2-normalized rows. G in R^{588 x 768} = frozen gallery image embeddings, L2-normalized. Score = G @ q (cosine, since both unit norm); rank descending. n=30 eval queries each with exactly ONE positive image.

MECHANISM (per eval query q_orig, casual Korean text):
1. LLM generation: feed q_orig to EXAONE/Qwen with a prompt that asks for K short paraphrases / formal catalogue-style rephrasings. K ~ 5-15. Keep them SHORT (phrase-length, like a product caption), not full HyDE captions. Set p_0 := q_orig itself; p_1..p_K := generated rephrasings. So K+1 strings.
2. Encode each with the SAME text tower used for indexing-side queries (the LoRA-adapted text tower if that is the deployed query encoder; must match how G's matching text would be encoded). e_j = text_encoder(p_j) in R^768. Then L2-normalize each: u_j = e_j / ||e_j||_2.
3. Mean-pool (the CLIP/CuPL ensemble): m = (1/(K+1)) * sum_{j=0..K} u_j.  (Optionally weighted: m = w0*u_0 + (1-w0)/K * sum_{j>=1} u_j, w0 ~ 0.5-0.7 to anchor on the original casual query — RECOMMENDED here, see gotchas.)
4. Re-normalize: q_ens = m / ||m||_2.   <-- this is the load-bearing step; cosine of a mean of unit vectors is NOT the mean of cosines, and re-normalization makes scores comparable.
5. Score and rank: s = G @ q_ens (length 588), argsort descending -> ranked product list for this query.
6. Metrics: R@1/5/10 + MRR over the 30 queries; bootstrap CIs by resampling the 30 queries with replacement.

ALTERNATIVE FUSION (do NOT default to this, but cheap to also try): instead of embedding-average, score each u_j separately against G and combine ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF: score_d = sum_j 1/(60+rank_j(d))). RRF is more robust to one bad paraphrase than embedding-mean but loses the variance-smoothing that is the whole point here. For single-positive MRR, embedding-mean with original-query anchoring (w0>0) is the right primary variant.

Qb (~7000 query bank) plays NO role at inference for this method (it is a training asset for the LoRA). The only optional use: pick K and w0 by tuning on a held-out slice of Qb-style queries with synthetic positives — but with N=30 and no labeled bank positives, just fix K~8, w0~0.6 a priori and report; do NOT tune on the 30 eval queries.
verdicts.gotchas:
CRITICAL DIRECTION MISMATCH vs CuPL/CLIP-ensemble: those papers average over the CLASS side (gallery side) where the target is a single fixed concept and paraphrases are near-synonyms — averaging cleanly denoises. Here you average the QUERY side. For a SHORT_AMBIGUOUS casual query, LLM paraphrases can DRIFT semantics (invent attributes: color, fit, occasion), pulling q_ens AWAY from the true single positive. Mean-pooling then regresses the query toward a blander centroid — this can HURT exactly the short_ambiguous bucket the project cares about, and helps least where the query is already clean (long_specific). Net effect on MRR is plausibly small and could be negative; mitigate with original-query anchoring (w0~0.6) so you can never do much worse than the LoRA baseline.

NORMALIZATION TRAP: if you skip per-paraphrase L2-norm before averaging, longer generations with larger raw norms dominate the mean. Must normalize-then-average-then-renormalize.

ENCODER-MATCH TRAP: encode paraphrases with the deployed query text tower (the LoRA tower, since baseline best = LoRA MRR ~0.68). Mixing frozen-encoded paraphrases into a LoRA pipeline is a silent bug.

HALLUCINATION: lower than full HyDE (short outputs), but EXAONE/Qwen still inject Korean fashion attributes not in the query; this is the main downside risk. Filter trivially-empty or English outputs.

STATISTICAL POWER: N=30 single-positive with already-wide CIs. A variance-reducer mainly tightens CIs but the point estimate move will likely be within the existing CI -> you probably CANNOT show a significant win over LoRA. As a NOVELTY claim it is weak: it is the textbook CLIP ensemble trick re-pointed at the query, reviewers will see it as incremental. Its honest role is a cheap fallback / ablation / HyDE-variance-control component, NOT a headline novel method.

OVERLAP WITH USER'S EXISTING WORK: this is query-side only and training-free, so it does not duplicate the failed learned reranker/ColBERT; but it is close in spirit to HyDE (same generate-then-encode family), so report them as one family with this as the low-hallucination short-generation variant.

verdicts.name: Mined hard-negative LoRA with SimANS ambiguous-band sampling + attribute denoising (cross-modal adaptation)
verdicts.citation_real: SimANS: Simple Ambiguous Negatives Sampling for Dense Text Retrieval. Kun Zhou, Yeyun Gong, Xiao Liu, Wayne Xin Zhao, Yelong Shen, Anlei Dong, Jingwen Lu, Rangan Majumder, Ji-Rong Wen, Nan Duan. EMNLP 2022 Industry Track, pp.548-559 (arXiv:2210.11773; aclanthology.org/2022.emnlp-industry.56). Code: github.com/microsoft/SimXNS. EXISTENCE CONFIRMED via abstract + multiple independent secondary sources; well-cited. HONEST CAVEAT: the 5.4MB PDF would not parse through WebFetch, so I could NOT byte-verify the equation constants. Well-attested mechanism: negatives ranked AROUND the positive are most informative and least likely to be false negatives; SimANS samples each candidate negative d_i from the retrieval top-k with weight p_i proportional to exp(-a*(s(q,d_i) - s(q,d+) - b)^2), s=relevance score, d+=positive, a=Gaussian sharpness, b shifts the peak just below the positive to suppress true near-duplicates. Loss = contrastive/InfoNCE over {positive} ∪ {sampled negatives}; mining iterative. Read exact a/b defaults + sampling routine from the SimXNS repo before implementing rather than trusting recalled constants.
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
VERIFIED ASSETS (read from disk). data/novel_cache/: shared__gallery_emb.npy=588x768 L2-norm TEST gallery; {base,lora384}__bank_q.npy=~7023x768 synthetic-bank queries; __val_q.npy(720)/__val_doc.npy(240)+meta.val_gt = held-out HP-tuning split; __eval_q.npy(30)+meta.eval_gt/eval_diff. data/vision_emb.npy+vision_idx.json = frozen vision emb for ALL products (lib.load_data subsets it to test AND to a 240-train val gallery -> TRAIN product images ARE embedded, the mining pool exists). data/train_pairs_final.jsonl = 7023 rows {product_id, query, query_type 1/2/3=short/med/long}. Attribute parser: src/attribute_rerank.py extract_facets over color/garment/sleeve/pattern/fit/neck Korean vocab. Eval+stats: src/novel/lib.py (ranks_of, metrics_at_k, bootstrap_ci, paired_compare, select_eval, load_caches). Train loop to extend: src/train_lora.py CLS path. Run env: /opt/miniconda3/envs/jolnon/bin/python (numpy+torch). cos==dot (rows L2-norm).

CRITICAL ADAPTATION — text->IMAGE, not the paper's text->text. SimANS mines negative DOCUMENTS from the corpus the query targets; here documents = product IMAGES, so negatives are OTHER product images, NOT other queries. The bank Qb is the TRAIN QUERY SET, never a negative pool (wrong modality). Qb only feeds in-batch negatives (other queries' positive images), already done by train_lora.py's (B,B) matrix.

MATH (single positive). Encode bank query j with text-LoRA -> q_j (768,L2). Gtr (Ntr,768,L2) = vision_emb rows for train pids in train_pairs_final MINUS the 588 test pids (defensibility: never a test image as train negative). pos[j]=Gtr row of query j's gold pid.
STEP1 (~1s): S=Qbank_lora @ Gtr.T; spos_j=S[j,pos[j]].
STEP2 (~1s): pool_j=top-k of S[j] (k≈100) minus pos[j]; w_i=exp(-a*(S[j,i]-spos_j-b)^2). SET a FROM DATA (SigLIP cosines compressed): σ=std of (S[j,pool]-spos_j); a≈1/(2σ^2); b≈-0.5σ. Sample m≈5 negs/query w/o replacement ∝ w_i.
STEP3 DENOISE with metadata, NOT LLM: drop sampled neg i if extract_facets(caption[i])==extract_facets(caption[pos[j]]) on every facet query j mentions. Catches attribute-twin false negatives. SKIP EXAONE/Qwen LLM-denoise (attributes cleanly parseable; LLM over 7023*m pairs = latency+hallucination for ~0 gain).
STEP4 retrain LoRA (minutes, 1 A6000, vision frozen/cached): extend train_lora.py CLS path. Per batch query gather from frozen Gtr (no grad): positive + m denoised explicit negs + in-batch other-positives; per-query logit row=logit_scale*[q.g+ , q.g_neg1..m , q.g_inbatch...]; InfoNCE label=positive. Keep existing symmetric in-batch term; append m explicit-negative columns to the text->image denominator. Re-mine once after ~1 epoch.
EVAL: lib.encode_text(eval)->score vs 588 gallery->lib.summarize + lib.paired_compare vs current LoRA. Tune k/m/a/b ONLY on cached val split (val_q/val_doc/val_gt); NEVER the 30 eval queries.
verdicts.gotchas:
RAN THE GO/NO-GO DIAGNOSTIC (current lora384, 30 eval queries vs 588 gallery, attribute-facet analysis of every item ranked above the gold). RESULTS: overall MRR 0.720, R@1 0.633, R@5 0.833, R@10 0.90. Only 11 misses (rank>1). Of those: 6 attribute-TWIN-blocked, 5 SEMANTIC/category-blocked. KEY PATTERN by rank: the recoverable near-misses (rank 2-3, n=6) are 5/6 TWIN; the deep misses (rank 11/16/26/41) are mostly SEM. So attribute-twin confusion IS real and dominates exactly the band where hard-negative training can help — but it is only ~half of all failures and the headroom is tiny (R@1 already 0.633; lifting the 5 rank-2/3 twin misses to rank 1 is the entire realistic upside).

UPSIDE CEILING IS SMALL AND CI-BOUND. Best case the 6 twin misses go to rank 1: R@1 0.633->~0.83, MRR ~0.72->~0.84. But with N=30 the bootstrap CI on MRR is roughly +/-0.13-0.16, so even a near-perfect twin-fix likely does NOT separate from the current LoRA at 95%. Realistically you recover 2-4 of those 6 -> a few MRR points, inside CI. Same non-separating regime where the FAILED learned reranker / dual-tower already landed; SimANS is in that training-side family.

DANGERS:
1. FALSE-NEGATIVE TRAP. The SimANS band in a templated near-dup catalogue is dominated by exact-attribute twins; for the short_ambiguous queries those twins are often legitimate answers (the diagnostic shows 3/4 short_ambiguous misses are TWIN). Pushing them down can REGRESS that bucket. Attribute-denoise is load-bearing, not optional.
2. COSINE-SCALE TUNING NULLS EASILY. Paper a/b are for dot-product range; SigLIP cosines compressed -> set a from empirical σ or sampling collapses to uniform (no effect) or onto the single top twin (false-neg trap).
3. SETUP: needs TRAIN-image negative pool (Gtr from vision_emb.npy minus 588 test pids), not the cached test/val galleries. Excluding test pids is mandatory (leakage).
4. VIOLATES USER PREFERENCE ORDER. User STRONGLY prefers training-free/test-time. This is retrain + mining + denoise = more moving parts, for upside in the marginal/CI-bound regime.
5. IN-BATCH NEGATIVES ALREADY APPROXIMATE IT over a templated corpus, so incremental value over big in-batch is smaller here than in the paper's web-scale setting.

VERDICT = MAYBE (leaning skip for the headline metric, worth it for the writeup). The mechanism is genuinely targeted at a confirmed failure mode (attribute-twin near-misses), but the realistic R@1/MRR gain is small and very likely inside the wide N=30 CIs, and a cheaper TEST-TIME attribute rerank already exists in the repo (attribute_rerank.py) that addresses the SAME twin misses without retraining — prefer that first. Pursue SimANS only if: (a) the test-time attribute rerank under-delivers, and (b) you want the cross-modal-hard-negative novelty story for the report. NOVELTY FRAMING (addresses 'no novelty'): SimANS is text-text dense retrieval; the novel adaptation is CROSS-MODAL ambiguous-band hard-negative mining over FROZEN image embeddings with attribute-metadata denoising for a near-duplicate fashion catalogue — distinct from the dismissed BM25-rerank methods and defensible even if the metric delta is small.

verdicts.name: Mutual Proximity (empirical/rank, cross-modal adaptation)
verdicts.correct_mechanism:
CONFIRMED REAL. Schnitzer, Flexer, Schedl, Widmer (2012) JMLR 13:2871-2902, "Local and Global Scaling Reduce Hubs in Space". MP recasts a similarity/distance into a probability that the relationship is MUTUAL. Original (symmetric, same-space kNN): for objects x,y with distance d_xy and per-object distance distribution to all other points, MP(d_xy) = P(X > d_xy AND Y > d_xy). Empirical estimate = fraction of objects z that are simultaneously farther from x than y is AND farther from y than x is. Independence approximation: MP = P(X > d_xy) * P(Y > d_xy). Works on distances (large=far); with cosine sims use s as similarity (large=near) and flip the inequality direction.

CROSS-MODAL ADAPTATION (text->image). Asymmetric: the two "marginals" live in different spaces, so you MUST source them from different banks (this is structurally identical to inverted-softmax / QB-Norm, just rank-based instead of softmax-based).
Inputs: Q (n,768 L2-norm) eval queries, G (588,768 L2-norm) gallery images, Qb (m~7000,768 L2-norm) bank queries.
Precompute (seconds, all numpy):
  S   = Q  @ G.T          # (n,588)   eval-query x gallery sims (the scores to rerank)
  Sb  = Qb @ G.T          # (m,588)   bank-query x gallery sims (for IMAGE-side marginal)
For a (query i, image j) pair with score s_ij = S[i,j]:
  1) Query-side factor P_q = fraction of GALLERY images that query i likes LESS than image j
       P_q(i,j) = (#{k in 588 : S[i,k] < s_ij}) / 588
     = (rank of image j among the 588 gallery sims for query i), normalized to [0,1]. This is just the within-row rank of s_ij -> monotonic in the original score, so ALONE it changes nothing.
  2) Image-side factor P_d = fraction of BANK queries whose sim to image j is LESS than s_ij
       P_d(i,j) = (#{q in m : Sb[q,j] < s_ij}) / m
     This is the hubness term: it down-weights gallery images j that are highly similar to MANY bank queries (universal hubs), exactly the QB-Norm/inverted-softmax signal but expressed as an empirical CDF / column-rank of s_ij within image j's bank-similarity distribution.
  3) MP score: MP(i,j) = P_q(i,j) * P_d(i,j)   (independence form). Rerank images j for query i by descending MP.
Vectorized P_d: for each column j sort Sb[:,j] once; P_d[i,j] = searchsorted(sorted_Sb[:,j], S[i,j]) / m. O(n*588*log m), runs in well under a second.
KEY EQUIVALENCE: because P_q is a monotone transform of the row score, the ONLY thing that re-ranks within a query is P_d (the bank-CDF / image-popularity term). So cross-modal "MP" here degenerates to: rerank by s_ij * P_d(i,j), i.e. multiply each score by the empirical bank-CDF of the gallery image. This is a rank/CDF-flavored variant of inverted-softmax with a multiplicative (not subtractive/divisive-softmax) combination. The symmetric "fraction of z farther from BOTH" joint-empirical form is NOT cleanly defined cross-modally; use the independence/product form.
verdicts.gotchas:
1) NOT INDEPENDENT FROM EXISTING METHODS. After the cross-modal reduction, MP reranks purely on the image-side bank-CDF term P_d -- the exact same "is this image a hub for the bank queries" signal that QB-Norm and inverted-softmax already use. The "second distinct hubness baseline" framing is half-true at best: it is the SAME hubness signal (bank-estimated image popularity) wearing a rank/CDF mask instead of a softmax mask. A reviewer who knows hubness will say "this is inverted-softmax with empirical CDF instead of softmax." So it does NOT meaningfully test robustness of the QB-Norm story; it largely re-derives it.
2) The query-side factor P_q is a within-row monotone transform => contributes ZERO to within-query ranking. So half of MP's machinery is inert here. Only image-side hubness survives. This guts the "doubly-symmetric" selling point in the cross-modal case.
3) N=30 single-positive eval, gallery 588. With one positive per query, R@k/MRR move in coarse quantized steps; bootstrap CIs are very wide. A hubness rerank helps only the subset of the 30 queries whose true positive was being suppressed by a hub image AND where the hub correction does not also demote the true positive. Realistically that is a handful of queries; the expected MRR delta is small and very likely inside the bootstrap CI -> "no significant difference" is the most probable outcome, same risk profile as plain QB-Norm/CSLS.
4) Empirical-rank variant has NO hyperparameter to tune (good for honesty), but also no temperature/beta knob, so you cannot dial strength; if the multiplicative P_d is too aggressive it can demote correct-but-popular items (fashion top-wear has genuinely popular generic items like white tees) with no way to soften it short of P_d^gamma, which then becomes a tuned knob on N=30 = overfitting risk.
5) Bank-CDF estimate per image uses m~7000 bank queries -> statistically fine per column.
